rel: The Quran was first collected into one book in Hazrat Abu Bakr's (R.A.) time on Hazrat Umar's (R.A.) advice.

question: In which year did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) migrate to Madinah?
why: The Hijrah to Madinah took place in 622 AD and marks the start of the Islamic calendar.
rel: The first revelation came in 610 AD and Makkah was conquered in 630 AD.

question: If your mother is my sister, what am I to you?
why: Your mother's brother is your maternal uncle (mamoon).
rel: Your father's brother is your paternal uncle (chacha).
note: Notes' wording ('my brother is sister of your mother') does not make sense; rewritten to fit the printed answer 'Uncle'.

question: The Cholistan Desert is mainly located in which district of Punjab?
why: Most of the Cholistan Desert lies in Bahawalpur district; it also extends into Bahawalnagar and Rahim Yar Khan.
rel: Derawar Fort is a famous landmark in Cholistan.

question: What is one-third of 10% of 90?
why: 10% of 90 = 9, and one-third of 9 = 3.
rel: 10% of a number is found by dividing it by 10.

question: What is one-third of 10% of 120?
why: 10% of 120 = 12, and one-third of 12 = 4.
rel: One-third of 120 directly is 40.

question: What is a quarter of one-tenth of 120?
why: One-tenth of 120 = 12, and a quarter of 12 = 3.
rel: A quarter means 1/4 or 25%.

question: Which is the longest tunnel of Pakistan?
why: The Lowari Tunnel (about 8.5 km main tunnel) linking Dir and Chitral is Pakistan's longest tunnel.
rel: The Khojak Tunnel (about 3.9 km) is Pakistan's longest railway tunnel.
note: Notes gave 'Hakla-Yarik Tunnel / Lowari Tunnel'; Hakla-Yarik is a motorway, not a tunnel. Lowari is the longest.

question: How many daughters did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) have?
why: The Prophet's daughters were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (R.A.).
rel: All his children except Ibrahim were from Hazrat Khadija (R.A.).

question: What title is given to the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) in the Quran (Surah Al-Anbiya 21:107)?
why: The Quran says: 'We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds' (21:107).
rel: Ruhullah is the title of Hazrat Isa (A.S.).

question: How many sugar mills did Pakistan have in 1947?
why: At independence Pakistan had only 2 sugar mills; most industry was in India.
rel: Today Pakistan has around 80-90 sugar mills.

question: What is the rate of Zakat on silver?
why: Zakat on gold, silver and cash is 2.5% (one-fortieth) of the wealth held for one year.
rel: The Nisab of silver is 52.5 tolas.

question: In which city is PIMS hospital located?
why: PIMS (Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences) is in Islamabad.
rel: Mayo Hospital in Lahore is one of the oldest hospitals in Pakistan.

question: Which city is called the 'Manchester of Pakistan'?
why: Faisalabad is called the Manchester of Pakistan because of its large textile industry.
rel: Faisalabad was earlier called Lyallpur.

question: 'Islamabad' is which type of noun?
why: Islamabad is the name of a particular place, so it is a proper noun.
rel: Proper nouns always begin with a capital letter.

question: In which direction of Pakistan is China situated?
why: China lies to the north (north-east) of Pakistan, bordering Gilgit-Baltistan.
rel: The Pak-China border is about 600 km long.

question: In which year was Mangla Dam completed?
why: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River was completed in 1967. Tarbela was completed in 1976.
rel: Mangla Dam is in Mirpur, Azad Kashmir.

question: What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan?
why: Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan.
rel: Skardu is the main town of Baltistan.

question: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with:
why: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway is the border crossing between Pakistan and China.
rel: The Karakoram Highway is called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.

question: Which is the world's largest desert lake?
why: Lake Turkana in Kenya is the world's largest permanent desert lake.
rel: Lake Turkana is also the world's largest alkaline lake.

question: Who is the head of state of Japan?
why: Japan has no president; it is a constitutional monarchy where the Emperor is head of state and the Prime Minister heads the government.
rel: Japan's parliament is called the Diet.
note: Notes item was 'President of Japan: Japan does not have a president'; rewritten as a head-of-state question.

question: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with:
why: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar (Pakistan) with Afghanistan via Torkham.
rel: The Bolan Pass in Balochistan links Sibi and Quetta.

question: What is the antonym of 'wild'?
why: Wild means not controlled by humans; the opposite is tame (domesticated).
rel: 'Domesticated' animals are those kept by humans, such as cows and goats.

question: Which is the largest international airport in the world by area?
why: King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, covers about 776 sq km, the largest by area.

question: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place?
why: The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4-5 February 1922; after it Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

question: When was the SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation) established?
why: The SCO was formed in Shanghai on 15 June 2001.
rel: Pakistan and India became full members of the SCO in 2017.

question: Which line marks the border between Pakistani Punjab and Indian Punjab?
why: Sir Cyril Radcliffe drew the boundary between Pakistan and India in 1947.
rel: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

question: In which year was the NATO treaty signed?
why: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April 1949 in Washington, D.C.
rel: NATO's headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium.
